N-R-rauch.objects: Normal Jacobi fields along one specified unit-speed geodesic in dimension at least two.
N-R-rauch.domain: The time lies strictly below both T and D_k; the lower-curvature branch also requires no actual conjugate point through T.
N-R-rauch.fixed_and_variable: The metric, ray, real k and positive initial derivative norm a are fixed; J and admissible time vary.
N-R-rauch.hypotheses: Each radial two-plane obeys the selected sectional bound throughout the segment; completeness is absent and unnecessary here.
N-R-rauch.equations: J(0)=0, derivative norm a, and the scalar initial-value problem s double prime plus k s=0 define the comparison.
N-R-rauch.quantifiers: Every admissible time is covered, separately under the two curvature hypotheses.
N-R-rauch.conclusion: Upper curvature gives longer fields; lower curvature gives shorter fields with the actual-conjugate restriction.
N-R-rauch.status: Established constant-model specialization; singular matrix comparison is an imported input.
N-R-rauch.local_definitions: Normal Jacobi equation is supplied in N-D-jacobi; s and D_k occur in the principal itself.

N-R-hessian.objects: The bilinear distance Hessian at an uncut point of a complete connected n-manifold.
N-R-hessian.domain: Positive distance ell is below D_k and x excludes the base point and cut locus.
N-R-hessian.fixed_and_variable: Fix metric, p, k and x; every tangent vector X is tested.
N-R-hessian.hypotheses: A bound for every radial two-plane along the unique minimizing ray is sufficient.
N-R-hessian.equations: The right side is s prime divided by s times the squared normal component, including dr(X).
N-R-hessian.quantifiers: The quadratic-form statement quantifies all X and states both sectional-bound directions.
N-R-hessian.conclusion: Sectional lower curvature yields the upper Hessian form; sectional upper curvature reverses it.
N-R-hessian.status: Established on the smooth distance domain, without any classical assertion across cut points.
N-R-hessian.local_definitions: The scalar initial-value problem and model cutoff are explicit; the adjacent Hessian operation identifies the bilinear form.

N-R-laplacian.objects: The scalar distance Laplacian on a complete connected manifold of dimension n at least two.
N-R-laplacian.fixed_and_variable: Fix g and k; every p and every point in its indicated regular domain are allowed.
N-R-laplacian.hypotheses: Ricci is bounded below by the same (n-1)k g globally.
N-R-laplacian.equations: Delta is div grad, and the model scalar equation and initial data are given.
N-R-laplacian.quantifiers: The bound holds for every base point and every indicated regular x.
N-R-laplacian.conclusion: An upper trace bound (n-1)s prime/s, not directional Hessian control.
N-R-laplacian.status: Established; the singular integrating-factor proof is local and scalar.
N-R-laplacian.local_definitions: r, model solution, D_k and Laplacian sign are stated in the block.

N-R-bishop-gromov.objects: Concentric metric-ball volumes relative to the complete simply connected n-dimensional space form.
N-R-bishop-gromov.domain: All finite 0<r<R, including saturation at the spherical diameter.
N-R-bishop-gromov.fixed_and_variable: Fix g and real k; p and the two radii vary.
N-R-bishop-gromov.hypotheses: Connectedness, completeness, smoothness, n at least two and Ricci lower bound are explicit.
N-R-bishop-gromov.equations: The comparison quotient and its initial value one are displayed; model volume is constant beyond pi/sqrt(k).
N-R-bishop-gromov.quantifiers: For every p and every ordered pair of positive finite radii.
N-R-bishop-gromov.conclusion: The normalized volume decreases and is at most one; the equivalent growth-ratio inequality has the correct direction.
N-R-bishop-gromov.status: Established. No broad rigidity or absolute noncollapse conclusion is incorporated.
N-R-bishop-gromov.local_definitions: The model is defined in the principal and its integral formula is provided in N-D-model.

N-R-myers.objects: A connected complete smooth manifold without boundary and its diameter and fundamental group.
N-R-myers.domain: Dimension n at least two; all points and tangent vectors.
N-R-myers.fixed_and_variable: One positive constant k works everywhere for the fixed metric.
N-R-myers.hypotheses: The global uniform positive Ricci lower bound is stronger than unspecified pointwise positivity.
N-R-myers.equations: Ricci_x(v,v) at least (n-1)k times squared norm is explicitly quantified.
N-R-myers.quantifiers: Every x and tangent v, followed by global conclusions for M.
N-R-myers.conclusion: Compactness, diameter at most pi/sqrt(k), and finite fundamental group.
N-R-myers.status: Classical theorem with the index-form calculation supplied; Hopf–Rinow and covering topology imported.
N-R-myers.local_definitions: The only nonstandard normalization is explicitly included in the inequality.

N-R-hadamard.objects: The exponential map from each tangent space to a connected complete nonpositively curved manifold.
N-R-hadamard.domain: The whole tangent space, for every base point; one-sheet conclusion adds simple connectivity.
N-R-hadamard.fixed_and_variable: The metric is fixed; p is arbitrary.
N-R-hadamard.hypotheses: Sectional nonpositivity and completeness give the covering; simple connectivity is conditional and not silently assumed.
N-R-hadamard.equations: The domain and codomain of exp_p are displayed.
N-R-hadamard.quantifiers: For every p; unique minimizing geodesic for every pair under the additional hypothesis.
N-R-hadamard.conclusion: Covering first, then global diffeomorphism and Euclidean topology in the simply connected case.
N-R-hadamard.status: Established; no replacement of sectional curvature by Ricci is claimed.
N-R-hadamard.local_definitions: Geodesic initial-value definition of exp appears at reader entry.

N-R-toponogov.objects: A chosen minimizing triangle and its SSS model, plus a same-angle model hinge.
N-R-toponogov.domain: Dimension n at least two; strict triangle inequalities and perimeter below 2D_k.
N-R-toponogov.fixed_and_variable: Fix g and k, choose p,x,y and their minimizing sides; later u,v vary along two chosen sides.
N-R-toponogov.hypotheses: Complete connected smooth boundaryless manifold with sectional curvature at least k.
N-R-toponogov.equations: Same-side lengths and matching distances from p are spelled out separately for SSS and SAS.
N-R-toponogov.quantifiers: Every angle and every pair of matching internal points are covered.
N-R-toponogov.conclusion: SSS actual angles and chords are at least model values; SAS actual opposite distance is at most model value.
N-R-toponogov.status: Established strict-perimeter form; gluing and chord conversion remain explicit imports.
N-R-toponogov.local_definitions: D_k, both comparison experiments and point matching are locally defined.

scope.evidence_basis: Actual author reading of each listed canonical block and the inherited mechanism bodies; recalculated Gram determinant, Wronskian, singular scalar boundary term, weighted quotient, sine index sum, convexity, differential scaling, Cauchy tail and auxiliary triangle perimeter. Source rereading is separately recorded; no mathematical node was changed.

findings: N-D-riemannian: The metric Gram determinant supplies volume and parallel orthonormal frames reduce covariant differentiation to component differentiation. The gradient represents df and the Hessian is the metric pairing of its covariant derivative; the Euclidean radial and normal eigenvalues are 0 and 1/r.

N-D-jacobi: Differentiating exp_p(t v(s)) gives A(t)w, while a vector w at tv gives A(t)w/t. Orthogonality produces diag(1,A^T A); A=tI+O(t^3) fixes the positive determinant sign before a zero and the pole S=t^{-1}I+O(t). Constant curvature solves A=s_k I.

N-M-riccati: Differentiating the zero Wronskian yields symmetry, then S prime equals minus curvature minus S squared. Singular matrix order is expressly imported from Remark 3.2. Its logarithmic length use includes the t=0 ratio and a contradiction excluding an earlier zero only for the upper-sectional branch.

N-M-geometric-inputs: Current X requires initial w=A^{-1}X; torsion freeness yields A prime A inverse and the radial Hessian vanishes. Hopf–Rinow, geodesic uniqueness, and connected-covering topology have precise distinct uses.

N-M-trace: The eigenvalue square inequality has the correct n-1 denominator. For u=a-c_k, mu is asymptotic to C t squared, so mu u tends to zero and integration gives the required sign. This step is scalar and does not invoke singular matrix order.

N-M-cut-integration: The preimage of an open ball is t<r and t<tau. The cut theorem supplies multiplicity one and a null complement. Zero extension decreases the normalized density, domination by one permits the angular limit, and local absolute continuity makes the almost-everywhere quotient derivative imply monotonicity at every radius. Myers closes only the positive model endpoint.

N-M-myers: Each sine trial field vanishes at both endpoints; summation turns curvature into Ricci and the two squared trigonometric integrals each equal L/2. Strict L>D_k makes a negative form. Completeness gives pairwise minimizing curves and compactness, including the lifted metric; closed discrete compact fibers are finite.

N-M-hadamard: One half of the second norm derivative equals derivative norm squared minus the curvature form. Convexity prevents a second zero. The radial/angular differential is injective. Entire radial pullback geodesics verify the one-point completeness criterion; inverse sections of a normal ball supply the full sheets, and simple connectivity removes multiple sheets.

N-M-toponogov: The map from a model normal ball contracts angular speed and preserves radial speed. The chord bound by (a+b+L)/2<R validates its use. Uniform nearby-center radii are needed at the limit. The exact 4/5 endpoint gluing import gives a 9/5 displacement bound and a summable Cauchy tail; all auxiliary triangle perimeters are bounded by the original P.

Boundary recalculation: on the flat cylinder, two lifts at angular arclength pi a give opposite one-sided distance derivatives despite J=tE. The thin-cylinder ball is bounded above by 2 pi epsilon times a Euclidean (n-1)-ball, so no absolute noncollapse follows.

The product of unit two-spheres has Ric=g in dimension four but zero mixed sectional curvature. Expanding cos(sqrt(k)c)=cos(sqrt(k)r)^2 gives c squared=2r squared-k r fourth/3+O(r sixth), confirming the directional and triangle boundary.

Rauch cutoff test: the curvature-two field vanishes at pi/sqrt(2), then is nonzero near pi while the curvature-one model tends to zero. The torus example has opposite model side 0.8 and actual distance 0.2. These are actual failures, unlike a mere missing reverse trace argument.
